title: Interfaces
description: Interfaces, implementations, and polymorphism in Java

exercises.title: Define Interface
exercises.description: Define interface Shape with Area() double method. Implement for Rectangle. Create rect = Rectangle{Width: 3, Height: 4}. Print Area().

exercises.title: Interface Satisfaction
exercises.description: Define Writer interface with write bytes. Implement for Logger with fmt.FSystem.out.printlnln. Create Logger and call Write.
hints: `Logger.write` returns length; `main` prints `n + " hello"` per reference.

exercises.title: Multiple Implementations
exercises.description: Define Shape interface with Area() double. Implement for both Circle (with Radius) and Rectangle. Create Circle{5} and Rectangle{3,4}, call Area on both, System.out.println the larger area.
hints: `Circle.area()` uses `Math.PI * radius * radius`; compare `double` areas with `Math.max` or a conditional.

exercises.title: Type Assertion
exercises.description: Define Describable interface with Describe() string. Implement for Person{name}. Create interface var, use type assertion to get Person and System.out.println name.
hints: Hold `Person` and print `p.name` — pattern matching is optional here.

exercises.title: Type Switch
exercises.description: Create a function describeAny(x Object) that uses type switch to System.out.println "int: <value>" for int, "string: <value>" for string, "unknown" for other types. Test with both an int and a string.
hints: Use `instanceof Integer i` / `instanceof String s` patterns (Java 16+) inside `describeAny(Object x)`.

exercises.title: Interface with Slice
exercises.description: Define interface Speaker with Speak() string. Implement for Dog (returns "Woaf") and Cat (returns "Mew"). Create a slice of Speaker with one Dog and one Cat, then call Speak on each.
hints: Implement `Speaker` on `Dog` and `Cat`; use `Speaker[]` or `List<Speaker>` and polymorphic `speak()`.

exercises.title: Empty Interface
exercises.description: Create a slice of empty Object containing: the int 42, the string "hello", and the float 3.14. Print each one's concrete type using a type switch.
hints: Print `float64:` for boxed doubles as in the sample.
